{{Top}}
[[File:SepCouncilUtapau-ROTS.png|thumb|right|250px|"Aliens" in the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[Separatist Council/Legends|Council]]]]
{{Quote|You refer to us as 'alien,' and the Princess calls us 'non-Human.' Why are we defined by you and in comparison to you?|[[Borsk Fey'lya]]|<ref name="X-Wing">''[[X-Wing: The Krytos Trap]]''</ref>}}
'''Alien''' was a (sometimes) [[Humanocentrism|Humanocentric]] biological&mdash;and sometimes political&mdash;term to describe a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] or a person of a species other than [[Human/Legends|Humans]] or some [[near-Human]]s. Moreover, it was sometimes applied to humans by other species.<ref name="Dark Force Rising">''[[Dark Force Rising]]''</ref> The term may have been derived from the first impression of early Humans, when they had their first contacts with species from other [[Planet/Legends|planets]]. However, it seems to have been prevalent even in subsequent millennia.

Since Humans were the most common and prominent sentient species in [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] affairs and history, they were often considered a standard or average to which the biology, psychology, and culture of other species were compared. Thus species with a body type roughly similar to Humans were often referred to as [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]].

Aliens were sometimes victims of [[speciesism]], being derided and avoided by Humans in certain societies, like [[Taris/Legends|Taris]] during the blockade of the [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Sith]]. Prejudice against aliens led many aliens and planets with alien native species to join the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], both times hoping for freedom and safety from prejudice.

==Behind the scenes==
The word ''alien'' originally meant "stranger," and came from the Latin word ''alienus'' of the same meaning. The word was directly borrowed into English, and frequently used in the sense of "foreigner," as in the [[Wikipedia:Alien (law)|legal term]] for a person who is not a native or naturalized citizen of the land where they are found. It was also used in biology to describe plant or animal species which were not naturally found in a given part of the Earth, but had been [[Wikipedia:Introduced species|introduced]] there.

The [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]] of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']] used the term '''not-men''' for aliens at one occasion.

In the twentieth century, the term was adopted to describe extraterrestrial intelligent life, whether in [[Wikipedia:Extraterrestrial life (popular culture)|fiction]] or in a more [[Wikipedia:Extraterrestrial life|scientific context]].
